prs.title: fix: handle EPIPE and ERR_STREAM_DESTROYED in StdioServerTransport
prs.author: kai-agent-free
prs.reason: [llm pick] cluster primary for issue #1564: Both PRs change 3 files and have unknown CI status, so the deciding factor is fix completeness. #1679 handles both EPIPE and ERR_STREAM_DESTROYED, whereas #1568 only handles EPIPE. In Node.js, ERR_STREAM_DESTROYED is thrown on the same write path when a stream is destroyed before a write completes — a scenario that occurs alongside EPIPE in StdioServerTransport. Catching only EPIPE (#1568) leaves ERR_STREAM_DESTROYED unhandled, meaning the process crash can still occur. #1679's broader error handling makes it the more complete fix for issue #1564.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs change 3 files and have unknown CI status, so the deciding factor is fix completeness. #1679 handles both EPIPE and ERR_STREAM_DESTROYED, whereas #1568 only handles EPIPE. In Node.js, ERR_STREAM_DESTROYED is thrown on the same write path when a stream is destroyed before a write completes — a scenario that occurs alongside EPIPE in StdioServerTransport. Catching only EPIPE (#1568) leaves ERR_STREAM_DESTROYED unhandled, meaning the process crash can still occur. #1679's broader error handling makes it the more complete fix for issue #1564.
